title: New warning on gift card scams amid holiday rush
description: ABC News' Becky Worley shares tips to protect your money as the FBI has warned that consumers are expected to lose $1 billion to gift card scams.

textual.observation: The report describes a gift-card tampering mechanism in which cards are removed from store racks, their numbers are recorded, replacement stickers are applied, and the balance is later drained after activation.

evidence.quote: A criminal could just pocket one of these cards inside a store
take that in total the strip right off and write down the numbers.

textual.context: Presented as an attributed warning and explanatory news report about gift-card scams, not as an instruction or endorsement.
textual.potential_relevance: The described access to gift-card numbers, replacement of visible packaging, monitoring for activation, and subsequent balance drain is a concretely described scam mechanism requiring later contextual assessment.
textual.limitations: These source records do not independently establish that the described mechanism occurred in every case, verify the reported figures, or establish the identity or intent of any person.

visual.observation: A news-style segment displays the headline “GIFT CARD WARNING” and the subheading “DEVIOUS SCAMS COULD COST CONSUMERS $1 BILLION,” alongside images of retail gift cards.
visual.context: Visible context is a Good Morning America / ABC consumer-alert news segment warning about gift card scams, not visibly promoting a gift-card offer.
visual.potential_relevance: The frames concretely present gift-card scams as a warning topic and link the scam mechanism to consumer cost risk, which is relevant for scam-related research while preserving the warning context.
visual.limitations: The sampled frames do not show the full spoken explanation, any specific scammer request, payment recipient, website, phone number, or individual transaction outcome.

visual.observation: A tip graphic titled “GIFT CARD TIPS” instructs viewers to “USE CREDIT CARD WITH FRAUD PROTECTION” and “BUY FROM MIDDLE OF RACK - EXAMINE MAGNETIC STRIP.” The lower banner says “HOW TO MAKE SURE YOURS HASN’T BEEN TAMPERED WITH.”
visual.context: Visible context is consumer-protection advice within the same gift-card warning segment.
visual.potential_relevance: The graphic describes a concrete protective action relationship: when buying gift cards, viewers are advised to use a fraud-protected credit card and inspect the magnetic strip because of possible tampering.
visual.limitations: The frame does not show an actual tampered card, how tampering is performed, or whether any specific card shown elsewhere was altered.

textual_context_notes.observation: The title and description frame the content as a warning intended to help consumers protect their money from gift-card scams.

visual_context_notes.observation: The segment uses Good Morning America / ABC News branding and repeatedly labels the content as a “GMA CONSUMER ALERT.”
The final sampled frame shows a platform-style end screen with “SUBSCRIBE NOW” and “KEEP WATCHING,” separate from the gift-card warning visuals.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as an ABC consumer-news warning that explains gift card scams and gives viewers advice to protect their money. The card-removal and number-recording mechanism is attributed to criminals as the subject of the report, while the video's own actions are protective, such as recommending fraud protection and inspecting cards for tampering. A separate end-screen subscription prompt does not establish a financial solicitation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary content is an anti-scam consumer warning: it describes a gift-card tampering and balance-draining mechanism attributed to criminals and gives viewers protective advice. It does not present that mechanism as an offer or instruction for viewers to carry it out.
